questions.question: The ratio of the cost price to the marked price of an article is 4 ∶ 7. A discount of 25% is given on the marked price and the shopkeeper made a profit of ₹50. Find the cost price of the article.

questions.solution:

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 50,000. Of three shopkeepers, the first one allows two successive discounts of 25% and 15%.The second one allows two successive discounts 20% and 20%. The third shopkeeper allows two successive discounts of 30% and 10%. From which shopkeeper does the customer get more profit?

questions.solution:

Effective discount = 30 + 10 - (30 × 10)/100 ⇒ 40 - 3 = 37%

questions.question: The marked price of a table lamp is Rs. 2,165. During the festive season, it is sold for Rs. 1,710.35. Find the percentage discount offered.
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a table lamp is Rs. 2,165. During the festive season, it is sold for Rs. 1,710.35. Find the percentage discount offered.
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price of a table lamp = ₹2165

Selling price during the festive season = ₹1710.35

Formula used:

Percentage Discount = ((Marked Price - Selling Price))/(Marked Price) × 100

Calculations:

Discount = 2165 - 1710.35

⇒ Discount = 454.65

Percentage Discount = (454.65)/(2165) × 100

⇒ Percentage Discount = 0.21 × 100

⇒ Percentage Discount = 21%

∴ The percentage discount offered is 21%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 12% on selling a book at 10% discount on the printed price. The ratio of the cost price to the printed price is:
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 12% on selling a book at 10% discount on the printed price. The ratio of the cost price to the printed price is:
questions.solution:
Cost price = (100 - discount%), Printed price = (100 + profit%)

Cost price = (100 - 10)  = 90. and Printed price = ( 100 + 12) = 112. 

Cost price : Printed price = 90 : 112  = 45 : 56.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked every item 25% above the cost price and allowed 10% discount. Shruti being a regular customer got 5% additional discount on the bill and paid Rs. 2394 for the item purchased. What is the cost price of the item (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marked every item 25% above the cost price and allowed 10% discount. Shruti being a regular customer got 5% additional discount on the bill and paid Rs. 2394 for the item purchased. What is the cost price of the item (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodEquivalent discount for Shruti = 10 + 5 - (10 × 5)/100 = 14.5%

Let the CP be Rs. 100

MP = 100 + 25 = 125

SP (For shopkeeper) = [125 × (100 - 14.5)]/100 = 106.875% = 2394

⇒ 1% = 22.40

⇒ 100% = Rs. 2240.

∴ The cost price is Rs. 2240.

Traditional method:

Given:

The Shopkeeper marked every item 25% above the cost price and allowed a 10% discount.

Shruti being a regular customer got a 5% additional discount.

She paid a bill of Rs. 2394.

Concept Used:

Percentage calculation

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the item purchased by Shruti be P.

Now,

Marked price

⇒ P + P × 25%

⇒ P (1 + 0.25)

⇒ (P × 1.25)

After 10% discount

⇒ (P × 1.25) - (P × 1.25) × 10%

⇒ (P × 1.25) (1 – 0.1)

⇒ (P × 1.25) × 0.9

⇒ (P × 1.125)

After addition 5% discount

⇒ (P × 1.125) - (P × 1.125) × 5%

⇒ (P × 1.125) (1 – 0.05)

⇒ (P × 1.125) × 0.95

⇒ (P × 1.06875)

According to the question,

(P × 1.06875) = 2394

⇒ P = 2394 ÷ 1.06875

⇒ P = 2240

∴ The cost price of the item purchased by Shruti is Rs. 2240.

questions.question: As part of Diwali offer, a jeweller allows a discount of 15%. Even after giving the discount, he makes a profit of 6.25%. Rani bought a gold chain which was marked at Rs. 5000 from this jeweller. Find the cost price of the chain for the jeweller.
questions.questionHtml: As part of Diwali offer, a jeweller allows a discount of 15%. Even after giving the discount, he makes a profit of 6.25%. Rani bought a gold chain which was marked at Rs. 5000 from this jeweller. Find the cost price of the chain for the jeweller.
questions.solution:
Discount = 5000 – S.P.

Discount% = (Discount /M.P.) × 100 ⇒ 15 = \(( 5000 - S.P.)\over5000\) × 100 ⇒ S.P. = Rs. 4,250

Profit = (4,250 – C.P.)

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 ⇒ 6.25 = \(( 4250 -C.P.) \over C.P.\) × 100 ⇒ C.P. = Rs 4,000.

questions.question: An article costs Rs. 4,000 to a shopkeeper, who marks its price at Rs. 8,400. The shopkeeper sells it to a customer at a discount of 25%. The customer gets a further discount of 15% on the discounted price if the customer redeems a coupon issued by the store previously. What is the profit percentage (to the nearest integer) earned by the shopkeeper in this transaction?
questions.questionHtml: An article costs Rs. 4,000 to a shopkeeper, who marks its price at Rs. 8,400. The shopkeeper sells it to a customer at a discount of 25%. The customer gets a further discount of 15% on the discounted price if the customer redeems a coupon issued by the store previously. What is the profit percentage (to the nearest integer) earned by the shopkeeper in this transaction?
questions.solution:
Final discount% = 25 + 15 - (25 × 15)/100 = 36.25%

Selling price of the article = 8400 × (1 - 36.25%) = Rs. 5355

Now, profit% = \(\frac {5355 - 4000}{4000} \times 100\%\) = 33.875% ≈ 34%

Difference between the discount = 3840 × 1.25% = ₹48

questions.question: If a discount of 10% is allowed on the marked price of an article. A shopkeeper gets a profit of 25%. If he offers a discount of 25% on the marked price of the same article, then his percentage profit/loss will be:
questions.questionHtml: If a discount of 10% is allowed on the marked price of an article. A shopkeeper gets a profit of 25%. If he offers a discount of 25% on the marked price of the same article, then his percentage profit/loss will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

D1 = 10%

D2 = 25%

Profit percentage = 25%

Calculation:

Let MP of the article be 100.

SP of the article = 100 × \(90\over100\) = 90

CP of the article = 90 × \(100\over125\) = 72

New SP of the article = 100 × \(75\over100\) = 75

Profit percentage = \((75-72)\over72\) × 100 = \(4\frac{1}{6}\%\) profit.

∴ The percentage profit is \(4\frac{1}{6}\%\).

questions.question: A car is sold on for successive discounts of 10%, 12%,15% and 20%. If the selling price of the car is ₹1,68,300, then what is the marked price of the car?
questions.questionHtml: A car is sold on for successive discounts of 10%, 12%,15% and 20%. If the selling price of the car is ₹1,68,300, then what is the marked price of the car?
questions.solution:
Given:

Successive discounts = 10%, 12%,15% and 20%

Selling price = SP = Rs. 1,68,300

Formula used:

Selling price = (1 - D1 / 100) x (1 - D2 / 100) x (1 - D3 / 100) x (1 - D4 / 100) x MP

Solution:

Let's put the values given, in the above formula,

1,68,300 = (1 - 10 / 100) x (1 - 12/ 100) x (1 - 15/ 100) x (1 - 20/ 100) x MP

1,68,300 = 0.9 x 0.88 x 0.85 x 0.8 x MP

MP = 168300/ 0.53856 = 312500

Hence, the Marked price is Rs. 3,12,500.

questions.question: An article is sold for Rs. 372 after two successive discounts of 25% and 38% on its marked price. Total discount (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: An article is sold for Rs. 372 after two successive discounts of 25% and 38% on its marked price. Total discount (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

SP of an article = Rs. 372

Discount % = 25% and 38%

Formula used:

Discount = Marked price –  selling price

Calculation:

Let the marked price be x

⇒ x × (100 – 25/100) × (100 – 38/100) = 372

⇒ x × (75/100) × (62/100) = 372

⇒ x × (3/4) × (31/50) = 372

⇒ x = 800

Now, Marked price = Rs. 800

Then, Discount = Rs. (800 – 372)

⇒ Rs. 428

∴ Total discount is Rs. 428

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 250. After allowing two successive discounts of 20% and x% on the marked price, it is sold for Rs. 185.60. What is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs. 250. After allowing two successive discounts of 20% and x% on the marked price, it is sold for Rs. 185.60. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
MP of the article = Rs. 250

SP of the article after getting 20% discount = 250 × 80/100 = 200

Final SP of the article = Rs. 185.60

Discount = 200 – 185.60 = 14.40

Discount % = (14.40/200) × 100 = 7.2%

questions.question: A single discount equivalent to a discount series of 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% is:
questions.questionHtml: A single discount equivalent to a discount series of 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A series of Discounts 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%

Formula Used: 

 Equivalent = A + B + (AB)/100

Calculation:

Discount is written as negative 

 Equivalent discount for 5% and 10% = (– 5) + (–10) + {(– 5) × (– 10)}/100

⇒ (– 5) + (– 10) + (0.5)

⇒ (– 15 + 0.5)

⇒ (– 14.5)

⇒ Equivalent Discount for 5% and 10% = 14.5%

Now, Equivalent discount for 14.5% and 15% = (– 14.5) + (– 15) + {(– 14.5) × (– 15)}/100

⇒ (– 14.5) + (– 15) + (2.175)

⇒ (– 29.5 + 2.175)

⇒ (– 27.325)

⇒ Equivalent Discount for 5%, 10% and 15% = 27.325%

Now, Equivalent discount for 27.325% and 20% = (– 27.325) + (– 20) + {(– 27.325) × (– 20)}/100

⇒ (– 27.325) + (– 20) + (5.465)

⇒ (– 47.325 + 5.465)

⇒ (– 41.86)

⇒ Equivalent Discount for 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% = 41.86%

∴  A single discount equivalent to a discount series of 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% is 41.86%.

Shortcut TrickCalculation:

Discount M.P S.P
D1 (5%) 20 19
D2 (10%) 10 9
D3 (15%) 20 17
D4 (20%) 5 4
Overall (D%) 20000 11628

Overall discount = (20000 - 11628) = Rs. 8372

Discount % = (8372/20000) × 100 = 41.86%

∴ The correct answer is 41.86%.

questions.question: The profit on selling an article for Rs. 1,100 is equal to three times the amount of loss on selling it for Rs 700. To gain 12.5% the article must be sold for:
questions.questionHtml: The profit on selling an article for Rs. 1,100 is equal to three times the amount of loss on selling it for Rs 700. To gain 12.5% the article must be sold for:
questions.solution:
Given:-

First S.P. = 1100

Second SP. = 700

Formula used:-

%Profit = [(S.P - CP)/CP] × 100

Calculation:-

Let CP of the article be x

According to the question

(1100 – x) = 3 (x – 700)

1100 – x = 3x – 2100

3x + x = 2100 + 1100

4x = 3200

x = 800

∴ SP of the article = 800 × (9/8) = Rs. 900

Shortcut Trick Calculation:-

4 unit = 400

1 unit = 100

3 unit = 300

CP = 800

∴ SP of the article = 800 × (9/8) = Rs. 900

questions.question: The cost price of a shirt is Rs. 1,008. At what price should it be marked so that after allowing 16% discount on the marked price, there is a profit of 18%?
questions.questionHtml: The cost price of a shirt is Rs. 1,008. At what price should it be marked so that after allowing 16% discount on the marked price, there is a profit of 18%?
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of the shirt = Rs. 1008

Formula used:

P = SP - CP     Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

SP = MP × (1 - D%/100)

SP = (1 + Profit%/100) × CP

Calculation:

Let the marked price of the shirt be X

According to the question

⇒ \({X\ × ({1\ -\ {16\over 100}})}\ =\ {1008\ × {118\over 100}}\)

⇒ 0.84X = 1.18 × 1008

⇒ 0.84X = 1189.44

⇒ X = \({1189.44\over 0.84}\ =\ Rs. 1416\)

∴ The required result will be Rs. 1416.

questions.question: Three shopkeepers A, B and C marked on an identical article at Rs. 4820. A, B and C sold their article on successive discounts of 20% and 20%; 25% and 15%; 30% and 10% respectively. Which shopkeeper gives the maximum discount and how much (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: Three shopkeepers A, B and C marked on an identical article at Rs. 4820. A, B and C sold their article on successive discounts of 20% and 20%; 25% and 15%; 30% and 10% respectively. Which shopkeeper gives the maximum discount and how much (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price of article = Rs.4820

Formula:

Total discount when a% and b% are successive discounts = (a + b) - (ab/100)

Discount amount = Marked price × discount%/100

Calculation:

Total discount for A = (20 + 20) - (400/100) = 36%

Total discount for B = (15 + 25) - (15 × 25/100) = 36.25%

Total discount for C = (30 + 10) - 300/100 = 37%

Discount for C = 4820 × 37/100 = Rs.1783.4

∴ From above, shopkeeper C gives maximum discount of Rs.1783.4

questions.question: The marked price of a trouser and a jacket is in the ratio of 1 ∶ 3. The shopkeeper gives 20 percent discount on the trouser. If the total discount offered on both of them together is 30 percent. then what is the discount percentage offered on the jacket?

questions.question: An article was sold for Rs. 512 after giving two equal successive discounts on the marked price of Rs. 800. The percentage discount offered is:
questions.questionHtml: An article was sold for Rs. 512 after giving two equal successive discounts on the marked price of Rs. 800. The percentage discount offered is:
questions.solution:
Given:

SP = Rs.512

MP = Rs.800

Calculation:

⇒ 512 = 800 × (100 - ? /100)

⇒ ? = 36%

Single discount = 36%

Let two equal discounts be a%.

⇒ 36 = (a + a - a2/100)

⇒ a2 - 200a + 3600 = 0

⇒ a2 - 180a - 20a + 3600 = 0

⇒ a(a - 180) - 20(a - 180) = 0

a = 180% or a = 20%

∴ % discount offered is 20%.

Shortcut Trick
According to the question, M.P = 800 and S.P = 512

Now, M.P : S.P = 800 : 512 = 400 : 256

Here, two equal successive discounts have given,

So, after one discount the ratio becomes,

⇒ M.P : S.P = √400 : √256

⇒ M.P : S.P = 20 : 16

Now, discount% is (20 - 16)/20 × 100 = 20%

questions.question: After allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price of an article, it was sold for Rs. 425. Had the discount not been given, the profit would have been 25%. What was the cost price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: After allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price of an article, it was sold for Rs. 425. Had the discount not been given, the profit would have been 25%. What was the cost price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling price = Rs. 425

Discount = 15%

And Profit % = 25%

Formula used:

Selling price(SP) = {(100 + Profit %)/100} × Cost price(CP)

Selling price = Marked price - Discount

Calculation:

Discount = 15% = 3/20

Let the market price be 20x And discount be 3x

SP = 20x - 3x = 17x

According to the question,

we get 17x = Rs. 425

⇒ x = 425/17 = Rs. 25

Now, Market price = 20x = 20 × 25 = Rs. 500

If MP = SP

⇒ CP × (125/100) = 500

CP = Rs. 400

∴ The cost price of the article is Rs. 400.

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers the following four schemes. Which scheme has the maximum discount percentage? a) Two successive discounts of 22% and 25% b) Buy 3, get 2 free c) Buy 5, get 4 free d) Buy 4, get 3 free
questions.questionHtml:
A shopkeeper offers the following four schemes. Which scheme has the maximum discount percentage?

a) Two successive discounts of 22% and 25%

b) Buy 3, get 2 free

c) Buy 5, get 4 free

d) Buy 4, get 3 free
questions.solution:
On considering condition (a), two successive discounts of 22% and 25% is net discount of (22 + 25 - 5.5) = 41.5%

On considering condition (b), we have buy 3, get 2 free, which means get 5 (MP) and pay only for 3 (SP) then discount% = 2/5 × 100 = 40%

On considering condition (c), we have buy 5, get 4 free, which means get 9 (MP) and pay only for 5 (SP) then discount% = 4/9 × 100 = 44.44% (MAX)

On considering condition (d), we have buy 4, get 3 free, which means get 7 (MP) and pay only for 4 (SP) then discount% = 3/7 × 100 = 42.85%

questions.question: A customer wanted to purchase an item marked for Rs. 10000. Shopkeeper offered two types of discounts, 25% flat discount or successive discounts of 14% and 12%. Which is the better offer for the customers and by how much?
questions.questionHtml: A customer wanted to purchase an item marked for Rs. 10000. Shopkeeper offered two types of discounts, 25% flat discount or successive discounts of 14% and 12%. Which is the better offer for the customers and by how much?
questions.solution:
Given:

An item purchased by customer = Rs. 10000

First types of discounts = 25%

Second types of discount = successive discounts of 14% and 12%.

Formula used:

Single discount on two successive discount = (a + b – ab/100)

Calculation:

According to the question

Single discount on two successive discount = (a + b – ab/100)

⇒ (14 + 12 – 14 × 12/100)

⇒ (26 – 1.68)

⇒ 24.32%

The best discount = First types of discount – Second types of discount

⇒ (25 – 24.32)% 

⇒ 0.68%

Now,

The better offer for the customers = Rs. (10000 × 0.68/100)

⇒ Rs. 68

∴ First offer by Rs. 68

questions.question: A trader marks his goods in such a way that even after allowing 15% discount on the marked price he still gains 27.5%. If the cost price of the goods is Rs. 200, then its marked price is:
questions.questionHtml: A trader marks his goods in such a way that even after allowing 15% discount on the marked price he still gains 27.5%. If the cost price of the goods is Rs. 200, then its marked price is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of the goods = 200

Discount = 15%

Gains = 27.5%

Formula used:

\({\rm{selling\;price}} = {\rm{\;marked\;price}} \times \frac{{100 - {\rm{discount\;percentage}}}}{{100}}\)

\({\rm{selling\;price}} = {\rm{\;cost\;price\;}} \times \frac{{100 + {\rm{gain\;percentage}}}}{{100}}\)

Calculation:

Let the marked price of goods be Rs. x

\({\rm{selling\;price}} = {\rm{X}} \times \frac{{100 - 15}}{{100}}\)

⇒ selling price = (85/100) × x

⇒ selling price = 0.85 × x      ----(i)

And \({\rm{selling\;price}} = 200{\rm{\;}} \times \frac{{100{\rm{\;}} + {\rm{\;}}27.5{\rm{\;}}}}{{100}}\)

⇒ selling price = 2 × 127.5

⇒ selling price = 255      ----(ii)

From equation (i) and (ii)

⇒ 0.85 × x = 255

⇒ x = 255/0.85

⇒ x = 300

Hence, the marked price of goods is Rs. 300.

 

Shortcut Trick Given, 

Discount percentage = 15%

Cost price = 200

Profit percentage = 27.5%

thus,

CP × (1 + Profit Percentage /100) = MP (1- Discount Percentage/100)

200× (1+27.5/100) = MP (1- 15/100)

MP = 300 Rs.

questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper buys an article at 30% discount on its marked price and sells it at 5% discount on its marked price. If he earns a profit of Rs. 65, then what is the marked price (in Rs.) of the article?

Given:

Profit = SP – CP

Calculation:

Let the MP be 100

According to the question

CP of an article at discount = 30% of 100

CP of an article = (100 – 30) = 70%

SP of an article at discount = 5% of 100

SP of an article = 95%

Profit = (95 – 70) = 25%

According to the question

⇒ 25% = 65

⇒ 100% = [(65 × 100)25]

⇒ Rs. (65 × 4)

⇒ Rs. 260

∴ The required MP is Rs. 260

questions.question: Amit purchased stationery marked for Rs. 8,000 at 12% discount and spent Rs. 160 on transportation. He sold the stationery at the marked price. Find his profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: Amit purchased stationery marked for Rs. 8,000 at 12% discount and spent Rs. 160 on transportation. He sold the stationery at the marked price. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Given

Market price = Rs 8000

Discount = 12%

Formula used

Cost price = Market Price - Discount

Profit % = \({profit\over cost price} \times 100\)

Calculation

Cost price = Market Price - Discount 

⇒ 8000 - 12% of 8000

⇒ 8000 - 960

⇒ Rs 7040

Total cost price =Rs( 7040 + 160)

⇒Rs 7200

Profit = Rs (8000 - 7200)

⇒Rs 800

Profit % = \({800\over 7200} \times 100\)

⇒ \(11{1\over 9} %\)

∴ Amit profit percentage is  \(11{1\over 9} %\).

questions.question: A person sells an article at 10% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 332 more, he would have made a profit of 20%. What is the original selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A person sells an article at 10% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 332 more, he would have made a profit of 20%. What is the original selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in profit/loss percentages = 20% − (−10%) = 30%.

Given that 30% of Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 332.

Multiplier for Original Selling Price (SP) at 10% loss = 90%.

Since 30% → 332, then 90% → 332 × 3 = 996.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 996.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial loss = 10%, New profit = 20%, Price increase = Rs. 332.

Formulas: SP = CP × (100 ± P/L%)/100 | Profit = SP − CP.

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

⇒ Original Selling Price (SP1) = 100 − 10 = 90 units.

⇒ New Selling Price (SP2) = 100 ± 20 = 120 units.

⇒ Difference (SP2 − SP1) = 120 − 90 = 30 units.

⇒ According to question, 30 units = Rs. 332.

⇒ 1 unit = 332 ÷ 30.

⇒ Original SP (90 units) = (332 ÷ 30) × 90 = 332 × 3 = Rs. 996.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 996.

Additional Information

Base for Profit/Loss

Unless stated otherwise, Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price of the article.

Percentage Gap Method

If an article is sold at x% loss and then at y% profit, the total difference in SP is represented by (x + y)% of the CP.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 625. After allowing a discount of 32% on the marked price, there was a profit of Rs. 25. The profit percentage (correct to the nearest integer) is:
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs. 625. After allowing a discount of 32% on the marked price, there was a profit of Rs. 25. The profit percentage (correct to the nearest integer) is:
questions.solution:
The selling price of the article = (100 - 32)/100 × 625 = (68/100) × 625 = Rs. 425

The cost price = 425 - 25 = Rs. 400, then profit = (425 - 400) = 25

The percentage of profit = (25/400) × 100 = 6.25% ≈ 6% (correct to the nearest integer)
